en: The Scripture of the Great Auspicious Meaning Dhāraṇī, Scroll One.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanyao, Director of the Bureau of Monastic Affairs under the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Homage to all Buddhas, the true deliverers of sentient beings, who have attained mastery over all dharmas. (7)
The Buddhas are truly the saviors Vipaśyin,
Śikhin, and Viśvabhū.
Kṛakucchanda, Kanakamuni,
and Kāśyapa.
The Lion of the Śākyas, the Honored One among two-legged beings, possesses great renown.
Maitreya dwells in the Tuṣita Heaven surrounded by a great assembly.
With a sincere heart, I call to mind all the Buddhas of the past.
All Buddhas of the future,
all Buddhas of the present who are unsurpassed Dharma Kings—
all such Buddhas of the three periods of time.
I take refuge in all; I take full refuge.
I take refuge in the Dharma, which is revered by all, and I take refuge in the Saṅgha.
This Sangha of monks is called the supreme field of merit;
even a small gift bestowed upon them yields a great reward.
All these Tathāgatas and Śrāvakas now take refuge in them.
Furthermore, I take refuge in Maheśvara who dwells in Akaniṣṭha;
I take refuge in the Śuddhāvāsa devas and all the Anāgāmin devas;
I take refuge in Brahmā, the King of Devas and progenitor of the world.
I take refuge in the Deva-king of Paranirmita-vaśavartin;
I take refuge in the Deva-king of Nirmāṇarati;
I take refuge in the Deva-king of Tuṣita.
I take refuge in the Heavenly King Suyāma;
I take refuge in Śakra, the Lord of Devas;
I take refuge in the Great Kings who protect the four quarters of the world.
I take refuge in all the spirits and deities who rely upon the earth.
I take refuge in all the nāgas and gandharvas,
and in all the kings of the desire realm, such as Indra.
Jvalanaprabha, Anantasoma, Parāvṛta, Śānta, and Śākyamuni—
to all such ones as these, I now take refuge. Also,
the two sages Nārada and Bādarāyaṇa.
Now I shall recite the mantra for the auspicious accomplishment of all purposes.
It binds the realm of ambrosial immortality and is capable of performing five hundred deeds.
It can cause all undertakings to be auspicious;
it can sever all malevolent spells and sorcery of the *gū* class;
and it can provide protection for the entire world.
It can cause all malevolent spirits and ghosts to retreat and disperse;
it can completely eliminate all those who inflict harm upon people;
and it can ensure that all undertakings are entirely auspicious and virtuous.
It can cause those who are evil to be filled with fear.
Those who wish to recite this mantra should do so with a sincere heart,
using exquisite incense, flower garlands, unguents, powdered incense, precious parasols, banners, and streamers.
They performed the subtle and exquisite sounds of singing, dancing,
and music as an offering to that World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Who Has Extinct Bonds,
who was pure and had severed all afflictions.
Gathering the mind in meditative concentration, it never wanders;
practicing the Four Great Vows, he rescues and protects all beings.
He utters a wondrous Brahma-sound that resounds afar like thunder.
Like the kalaviṅka bird, which is a joy for all to hear,
I pray that you accept my most supreme offering.
Homage to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present!
Homage to Vipaśyin Buddha,
Śikhin Buddha,
and Viśvabhū Buddha.
Karaṇagāndhāra Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha,
Kāśyapa Buddha, and Śākyasiṃha.
Maitreya is the foremost among the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in worlds throughout the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
acting as a great protector for all sentient beings.
If there are calamities or afflictions that can be rendered auspicious and favorable,
and if this is indeed so, I now offer this incense with utmost sincerity.
May these fragrant vapors reach the abodes of all Buddhas.
He then spoke the mantra:
*dacche, dache, ache, ache, mache, ache, nache, michi*. Having spoken this mantra, he burned various famous incenses, such as storax and benzoin.
Make offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time, the lions among men;
they shall always remember me with their blessings and protection.
Furthermore, with a sincere heart, burn various famous incenses, such as *sāgaraja* and *candana*.
Directing his mind toward making offerings to the Heavenly King Maheśvara, he prayed:
"May this fragrant incense reach that celestial palace.
He then spoke the mantra:
Nana nana nana | Rara rara rara | Hāri āri | Tiri sirāti | Riti suti | Furthermore, with a sincere heart, burn various kinds of incense, such as pi-kha (bikha) incense and others.
Directing his mind toward making offerings to the Māra King of the Desire Realm, who possesses great power and is the lord of the Desire Realm, he prayed:
"May this fragrance reach that king.
He then spoke the mantra:

Duò duò duò douní douní douní pīnà hēluó hēní tuóchí móní lídì. Furthermore, with a sincere heart, burn various famous incenses such as *vakkula* and others, and with a focused mind, make offerings to the Heavenly King of Nirmāṇarati and the various devas of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven.
"May this fragrance reach that king.
If he does not remember me, may his head split into seven pieces.
Then she spoke this mantra:
Nili niri niri mīri mīri mīri jile jile mijile mijile. Furthermore, with a sincere heart, burn various kinds of incense.
Directing his mind toward the offering to the King of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Emanations, he made this vow:
"May these fragrant scents reach that king;
may he remember me. Then he spoke the mantra:
Kare, vare, nare, hare, vinare, viśale, hara-mite svāhā. Furthermore, I now sincerely burn various kinds of famous incense.
Directing his mind toward the offering, he made this vow:
"May these fragrant scents reach the abode of the King of Tuṣita;
may he accept my offering."
Then he spoke the mantra:
*masi masi masi mamasi sarāmasi manasi haraṇi haphuha pharaṇi harī medite gandhū vahare svāhā*. Furthermore, I now burn various kinds of famous incense.
Directing the mind toward the offering to Suyama, the Heavenly King, together with his ministers and retinue,
may these fragrant scents reach that king’s abode.
Then he spoke this mantra:
KHATA KHANIATA KHATI VINI SACHI CHI SACHICHI DICHA PABHARI GANDHU PABHARA SVĀHĀ. Furthermore, burn various kinds of incense.
Directing his mind toward the offering to Śakra, the King of the Thirty-three Devas, he made this aspiration:
"May this fragrance reach the presence of that king.
He then spoke this mantra:

Hara hara māriṇi carasi li virasi li. Next, burn various kinds of incense and, with a focused mind, offer worship to the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the East, together with his ministers and retinue.
"May this fragrance reach the presence of that king.
Then he spoke the mantra:
*Āye vāye nāḍaye nāyani nānāna pade nipade parane svāhā*. Furthermore, burn various kinds of renowned incense.
Directing the mind toward the offering to the Great Heavenly King Virūḍhaka of the south, along with his ministers and retinue,
may this fragrance reach that king’s abode.
Then he spoke this mantra:
Viliśi viliśi jiliśi miliśi mini-liśi. Furthermore, burn various kinds of incense and, with a focused mind, make offerings to the Western Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, his ministers, and his retinue.
"May this fragrance reach the place where that king resides.
He then spoke the mantra:
*Dauṭi, bindauṭi, bindu, ḍimai, haḍimai-mai, mai-li, taimai-li, taima-ride, harade, svāhā.* Furthermore, he burned various kinds of famous incense.
Directing the mind toward the offering to the Northern Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa and his ministers and retinue,
may this fragrance reach the presence of that king.
Then he spoke the mantra:
KHAKHACI KHAKHACI KHAKHAKHACI KHAKHAKHACI MAKHACI MAKHACISI MATA HĀRINI. Furthermore, burn various kinds of incense.
Directing my mind, I offer this to Viśvānara, the lord of the rākṣasas within the city of Laṅkā on the island in the great ocean.
May these fragrant scents reach his presence.
Then he spoke this mantra:
Cali cali, cūli cūli, tili tili, varuṇili, varāhantini, harameṭi svāhā. Furthermore, burn various kinds of incense.
Directing his mind toward making offerings to Vemacitrin, the Asura King who dwells by the seashore, he made this vow:
"May these fragrant scents reach the abode of that king.
He then spoke this incantation:
Icchi vicchi vicchāci cchaṭṭale maṭṭale mamaṭṭa aramitī svāhā. Furthermore, burn various kinds of incense.
Directing the mind toward the offering for the Naga King Kāla, who dwells within the ocean, one makes this vow:
"May these fragrant scents reach the abode of the Naga King.
Then, one recites the mantra as follows:
Ka ka kali karani li karabariṇi viriśiri hara-mite svāhā. Furthermore, burn various kinds of incense.
Directing his mind toward making offerings to the Earth Deity,
he prayed that this fragrance might reach her abode,
and then spoke this incantation:
Vicinḍiri, Vibhañcetiḍiri, Caṇḍili, Śarameḍi, Māmarāreḍi, Āramiti, svāhā. If you do not believe my mantra.
Their hearts will split into seven pieces and blood will flow from their mouths;
if they do not listen to the wholesome Dharma taught by the Buddha,
they will never attain auspiciousness and will ultimately be slain by disease.
When his body perishes and his life ends, he shall fall into hell.
At that time, when the devas and asuras were engaged in mutual combat, Śakra’s army was defeated and retreated.
Having entered the city, he immediately had this thought:
I shall now go to the presence of the Bhagavān to seek his protection;
among gods and humans, the Buddha is the most supreme,
for he compassionately rescues and delivers all sentient beings.
He shall not harm any being and will always provide protection.
At that time, the World-Honored One was at Mount Upananda, his habitual place of delight,
together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.
At the time of the poṣadha on the fifteenth day of the month, there were a thousand nayutas of bodhisattvas;
it was then that the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings, the Supreme among Gods and Humans, appeared.
Surrounded by the fourfold assembly like a bright lamp in the world,
Śakra Devānām Indra, together with his retinue of hundreds of thousands of nayutas of Trāyastriṃśa gods,
came to where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to sit on one side, and with single-minded devotion joined his palms.
And he spoke in verse:
"Great Sage, Hero of the World, Honored One of Gods and Men, Ever with a compassionate heart you pity all beings.
Excellent, O All-Knowing Guide! You bring illumination to the darkness of the world."
"That which all the devas cannot comprehend, only Gautama alone knows it.
Now I take refuge in the Great Compassionate One; I pray only that you will grant me protection.
At that time, having heard this verse, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, saying:
"O Lord of Devas, within my Buddha-dharma there is a rite for binding the boundary through incantations (*dhāraṇī*),
which can provide great protection for humans and devas.
If anyone hears this rite for binding the boundary through incantations..."
Whether one upholds it oneself or teaches others to uphold it,
if one reads and recites it with a sincere heart and practices according to its teachings,
then by the power of the mantra, blades shall be unable to cause harm.
Poisonous fires cannot harm it; it can repel enemies for a hundred yojanas, and within this range there will be no calamities or afflictions.
Neither devas, asuras, nor any ghosts or spirits can transgress this boundary of the mantra to inflict ruin or injury.
Therefore, O Lord of Devas, you should receive and uphold this method of binding mantras.
You must read and recite it with a sincere heart and never allow it to be forgotten.
Then he spoke the mantra:
Jale jalinīma jale
Mahāśrī-mahāśarāvatī-ācāryaḥ
Ajali-jara-jali-jari-le.
Mare mare jara-te.
Cāraparati cārapati cārajapati
Naradevavarase ire ilavate.
Maimai mairāvatī hve hve mairi.
Vīriṃchiyūriḥ
Mahāśūrapati-makari.
Mahāmakarīharaśrīḥ
Vajrībhagavān yūro vārīḥ.
Vara-vasiri-vasiri-siri.
*Siri siriṇi*.
By this true mantra, may the sovereign be protected and all afflictions entirely removed.
I now extend loving-kindness toward that Dragon King, Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
The Naga King Cīrapaṇi,
the Naga King Virūpākṣa Kṛṣṇagautama,
and the Cintāmaṇi Naga King.
The Naga King Vaśuki, the Naga King Dhṛtarāṣṭra,
the Naga King Pūrṇa,
and the Naga King Nanda.
Possessing the majesty of name-and-form and a body of great stature, he dwells upon Mount Sumeru;
whenever the devas and asuras fight,
he constantly assists Śakra to provide protection.
The Dragon King Anavatapta,
the Dragon King Aruṇa,
and the Dragon King Pañcaśikha.
The Naga King Takṣaka,
the Naga King Ānandana,
and the Naga King Vāsuki.
The nāga kings beginning with Aparājita,
Mahāśvaravasu nāga king, and Īśvaravasu nāga king.
The Nāga King Nata-kien,
the Nāga King Aparaloka, and the Nāga King Samitakā.
The Naga King Dadhimukha;
furthermore, there is the Naga King Manasvin and the Naga King Pundarika.
The Dragon King Fangzhu,
the Dragon King Jiagoutuochi,
and the Dragon King Yanpoluo.
To the Naga King Aśvatara and to all such naga kings as these,
I give rise to a mind of loving-kindness.
To the Naga King Vāsuki...
The Nāga King Vīra, the Nāga King Romakaṇṭha,
and the Nāga King Uraga-kanaka.
To the Nāga King Ox-King, the Nāga King Dragon-King,
and all such nāga kings as these, I likewise give rise to a mind of loving-kindness;
as do I to the Nāga King Flapping-Ears.
The Naga King Ratha,
the Naga King Saṃcaya,
and the Naga King Sukhaprīti.
The Dragon King Vatsa, the Dragon King Elāpattra,
and the Dragon King Kṛṣṇabāli.
In this way, O Dragon King, I give rise to a mind of loving-kindness toward them all.
Likewise, toward those with one head, two heads, and so forth,
I give rise to a mind of loving-kindness toward them all.
In all worlds— whether they have feet or are footless, two-legged, four-legged, or many-legged—
he gives rise to a mind of loving-kindness toward them all.
Thus, for those nāgas, yakṣas, and others who are footless, two-legged, four-legged, or many-legged, [he acts accordingly].
And all those who depend upon the earth— whether moving or unmoving, including those born from roots—
may none of them harm me,
through the power of all the Buddhas.
And the Arhat of the majestic power of the True Dharma:
may they bring me peace and prosperity.
Then he spoke this mantra:
Dukimuki makimakamaki.
Ukkhamukkha parāti paravati dharī.
Dīrghapati svabhūriḥ.
Śvapano raṇavāriṇa radhipratiśukhabhaṇḍalikatacchi.
Katāpe katāpe cīulī śūlapaśi.
Śaurabha śivabha raśvabha naśi.
Aśe aśe śe ana-raspe.
Vara varaṇi cara carini.
Vijaranirvṛtāpade āpade.
Itaṭe aṭaṭale anaṭarade.
Ṭaṭṭe iṭṭe caṭṭe.
Vīṭape vīraparāta mahāra niri.
Varadāri varadāri pāgatari padana padana.
When Niṭalini-mai spoke this great king of mantras,
this great earth shook in six ways simultaneously throughout its entirety.
All the spirits, ghosts, asuras, and so forth—
They were all greatly terrified and said to one another:
"How strange! This Gautama of great renown preaches this divine mantra for the sake of the assembly of devas."
And thus cause all the devas to attain mastery.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
"Suppose a mantra-practitioner were to recite and maintain this mantra."
The boundary of the mantra is bound so as to pervade the triple world;
neither the moving nor the unmoving can transgress it.
The Heavenly Kings of the Four Quarters possess great majestic power.
His name is Maheśvara.
He abides in the noble fruit of an Anāgāmin.
Should anyone act contrary to this and transgress the boundary of this mantra, [they shall suffer].
This is impossible.
Mahābrahmā Deva-rāja possesses great majestic virtue;
as the lord of a thousand worlds, he possesses sovereign power.
If one could transgress this boundary of the mantra without compliance, such a thing is impossible.
Even Māra Pāpīyān, the lord of the desire realm,
would find it impossible to transgress the boundary of this mantra.
It is impossible for the King of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations or the King of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations to transcend this boundary of the mantra.
It is likewise impossible for the King of the Tuṣita Heaven or the King of the Yāma Heaven.
It is impossible for anyone to transcend this boundary of the mantra;
even Śakra, the thousand-eyed husband of Śacī,
cannot transcend this boundary of the mantra.
It is impossible for the four world-protecting kings— Kubera,
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūpākṣa, and Virūḍhaka—
to transgress this boundary of the mantra.
Furthermore, there are four kings of fierce and blazing power—
Kunāla, Gālandavyūha, Kucara, and Hārītī—
who cannot possibly transgress the boundary of this dhāraṇī; such a thing is impossible.
Furthermore, there are four kings who have attained the greatest sovereignty within the desire realm:
Śakra, Yama-rāja, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
It is impossible for anyone to pass beyond this boundary of mantras.
Furthermore, there are four kings of great power—
Candana, Vibhīṣaṇa, Jyotiṣprabha, and Vairocana—
who likewise have no power to pass beyond this boundary of mantras.
There are eight dragon kings who dwell in the great ocean and possess great majestic power:
the Dragon King Anavatapta,
the Dragon King Valuhana, and so forth.
The Naga King Virūḍhaka,
the Naga King Śubhara,
and the Naga King Citra.
The Nanda Dragon King, the Upananda Dragon King,
the Sāgara Dragon King, and others.
They possess great supernormal powers.
It is likewise impossible for dragon kings such as these to transcend the realm of this mantra.
There are eight asura kings.
The asura king Vemacitra, the asura king Śatadru,
and the asura king Rāhu.
The Asura King Śambhala, the Asura King Pralamba,
and the Asura King Mañjughosadharana.
Even if the Asura King Cāndaroṇa and others were to attempt to disregard this mantra or transgress its boundary, it would be impossible;
there is also a Gandharva King.

Citta, Roṣaṇa, Cūḍapanthaka, Jaṭāsandha, Śvabhū, Viśvabhū, Sattva, Śikhaṇḍin, Bhavatu, Dhūmra, Akṣobhya, Pañcaśikha, Gandharva, Pāpulu, Brahmadaṇḍa, Kāmaśrī, and Candana—these Gandharvas and others possess great supernormal powers.
He was handsome in appearance and possessed great renown;
yet, it would be impossible for him to transcend the realm of mantras.
The Buddha asked Śakra, Lord of Devas: "For what reason does this mantra possess such power?"
This mantra was spoken by the divine mouths of eighty-four billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of Ganges-sands of Buddhas;
I, now present, likewise proclaim this king of mantras.
He spoke again to Śakra, Lord of Devas: "Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well.
The power of this mantra can provide great protection for sentient beings, warding off all spirits and ghosts so that they do not harass or approach them."
This is why they provide protection.
Among these various paths of human beings,
it is capable of acting as the seed for rebirth in the heavens.
It can produce the superior retributions of all devas;
from this place, Buddhas emerge, from this place, śrāvaka disciples are born,
and from this place, the great virtuous ṛṣis are born.
This place gives rise to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas;
this place can give rise to spirits and ghosts.
If there are those who harass and disturb sentient beings, [they shall be subdued here].
It is able to ward off evil spirits so that they do not inflict harm;
therefore, this mantra is uttered.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

A-ra-che, vi-ra-che, ba-ra-che, ba-na-che, ba-ra-vi-ra-vi, dam-pi, dam-pi e-ji, pi-ta-ji vi-ra-ta-ji, shu-hui shu-hui, shu-ha-man-ta-li, ka-ra-che, shi-yu-li, kin-tou-mo-te, ta-ra, ta-li, ta-ra-ra-che, ta-ta-ba-vi, da-ta-ho-te, ra-sa-a-chieh-lo-ba-te, pin-tou-ka-li, ra-ta-na-sha-li. When this mantra was spoken, the great earth and the great oceans all shook in six ways.
All the spirits and deities raised a great cry of lamentation, exclaiming, "Alas,
what suffering! The rākṣasas did likewise,
saying to one another, "Now a mantra is being recited."
"We are in great suffering and seek a path from which there shall be no further birth.
Thus was this fierce mantra spoken by all the Buddhas.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Śakra, Lord of Devas, saying:
"You should now protect this realm of mantras.
Because of my protective mindfulness regarding these mantra conditions,
no humans or devas shall be able to transgress it."
He further addressed the Four Heavenly Kings of the Path’s Face,
who possess great renown and dwell among the Anāgāmins in the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens, named Maheśvara.
As well as their retinues, ministers, and high officials—
you all should protect this mantra with the supernatural powers and majestic virtue of the five Anāgāmin deities.
He is fully endowed with a physical form and a renowned name.
You and your retinue should likewise protect this vidyā-mantra.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, arose from a lotus.
Retinues and ministers,
you too should protect this mantra.
All devas from those of the four dhyānas up to the Brahmakāyika heaven.
Those endowed with supernormal powers, physical beauty, and renown,
as well as their retinues, ministers, and high officials,
should likewise protect this divine mantra.
Māra Pāpīyān, the lord of the desire realm, together with his retinue, ministers, and counselors,
should protect this mantra.
The King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, along with his retinue, ministers, and great officials, should also protect this mantra.
The King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, together with his retinue, ministers, and counselors, should protect this mantra.
The King of the Yama Heaven, together with his retinue, ministers, and counselors, should protect this mantra.
The celestial king Tuṣita, together with his retinue and attendants, shall protect this mantra.
Śakra, the thousand-eyed husband of Śacī, together with his retinue and attendants, shall likewise protect this mantra.
The Scripture of the Great Auspicious Meaning Divine Spell, Scroll One;
The Scripture of the Great Auspicious Meaning Divine Spell, Scroll Two.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanyao, Director of the Bureau of Monastic Affairs during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
The Four World-Protecting Kings govern the four directions. Dhṛtarāṣṭra governs the hosts of gandharvas;
he has ninety-one sons, all of whom are named Indras.
Of upright appearance and great majestic power,
his retinue and attendants shall likewise protect this mantra.
Virūpākṣa leads the hosts of kumbhāṇḍas.
The ninety-one sons were all named Emperors (*deva*).
They were handsome in appearance and possessed great power.
Their retinues and attendants shall likewise protect this mantra.
King Virūḍhaka leads the hosts of nāgas;
his ninety-one sons are all named Śakra.
Together with their retinues and associates, they shall protect this dhāraṇī.
King Vaiśravaṇa leads a host of yakṣas;
his ninety-one sons are all named Ti.
Together with their retinues and attendants, they shall protect this mantra.
These Four Heavenly Kings together have three hundred and sixty-four sons who are able to protect the ten directions.
Furthermore, there is a Heavenly Emperor named Indra;
next are the yakṣa and ghost hosts known as Lambā, Varuṇa, Soma, Brahmā, and Śarabha.
All of you should protect this mantra.
There are eight dragon kings:
the Dragon King Anavatapta and the Dragon King Baluṇa.
The Naga King Virūḍhaka, the Naga King Śubhara,
the Naga King Citra, the Naga King Nanda,
the Naga King Upananda, the Naga King Sāgara, and others.
The retinues and attendants should likewise protect this mantra.
There are eight asura kings:
the asura king Vemacitra, the asura king Śuci, and so forth.
The Asura King Rāhu, the Asura King Śambhali,
the Asura King Pralamba, and the Asura King Mañjughosha.
The Asura King Nataṇḍu, the Asura King Nata,
and their retinues and associates shall protect this mantra.
There is Śakra Devānām Indra, who presides over the four quarters.
Mahābrahmā Devarāja presides over the upper regions,
while Citta-rasana Gandharva-rāja and others diligently and tirelessly protect the realm of mantras day and night.
The yakṣa leaders Maṇibhadra and Pūrṇabhadra,
the long-armed and long-haired wilderness spirits (āṭavika).
Kalyāṇabuddhi, Vasu, Pañcika;
Dharmapāla, Dharmarakṣa, Dadhimukha; up to Śaraloma.
As well as Mahāmukha and the Jāṇika-ga;
such are these various spirits, endowed with supernormal powers, physical strength,
renown, and accompanied by retinues and ministers.
"May all of you protect those who uphold this mantra.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
*Jarāviṣi mahāsādame śubhaki pravaracite nirjase āsamī śuke āśmike damibipule.* When he spoke this mantra, the great earth shook violently.
The hosts of ghosts and spirits cried out,
"Alas, what suffering! All the rākṣasas likewise raised this cry,
